summary: A stack removes the newest item first (LIFO). A queue removes the oldest item first (FIFO). Python uses a list as a stack and collections.deque as a queue.
notes: stack.append() and stack.pop() both work on the end of the list, so they are O(1).
if not stack or stack.pop() != pairs[ch] checks for an empty stack first, so pop() never runs on an empty list.
print_queue.popleft() removes from the front of a deque in O(1). list.pop(0) does the same job in O(n).
pitfall: Calling pop() on an empty list raises IndexError: pop from empty list. Check if stack: before popping.
